question: Prove that $\tan^{-1}\frac{1}{5}+\tan^{-1}\frac{1}{7}+\tan^{-1}\frac{1}{3}+\tan^{-1}\frac{1}{8}=\frac{\pi}{4}$.
explanation:
First combine $\tan^{-1}\frac15 + \tan^{-1}\frac17$.

Using formula $\tan^{-1}A+\tan^{-1}B=\tan^{-1}\frac{A+B}{1-AB}$.

This gives $\tan^{-1}\frac{6}{17}$.

Next combine $\tan^{-1}\frac13 + \tan^{-1}\frac18$.

This gives $\tan^{-1}\frac{11}{23}$.

Now add $\tan^{-1}\frac{6}{17}+\tan^{-1}\frac{11}{23}$.

Using same identity we obtain $\tan^{-1}(1)$.

But $\tan^{-1}(1)=\frac{\pi}{4}$.

Hence the required sum equals $\frac{\pi}{4}$.

options.A: Combining $\tan^{-1}\frac15+\tan^{-1}\frac17$ gives $\tan^{-1}\frac{6}{35}$ and combining the remaining terms gives $\tan^{-1}\frac{11}{24}$, so the sum is $\frac{\pi}{6}$.
options.B: Combining $\tan^{-1}\frac15+\tan^{-1}\frac13$ gives $\tan^{-1}\frac{4}{15}$ and combining the remaining terms gives $\tan^{-1}\frac{15}{56}$, so the sum is $\frac{\pi}{3}$.
options.C: Combining $\tan^{-1}\frac15+\tan^{-1}\frac17$ gives $\tan^{-1}\frac{6}{17}$ and combining $\tan^{-1}\frac13+\tan^{-1}\frac18$ gives $\tan^{-1}\frac{11}{23}$. Adding these gives $\tan^{-1}(1)=\frac{\pi}{4}$.
options.D: Combining all four terms directly gives $\tan^{-1}\frac{1}{4}$, so the required sum is $\tan^{-1}\frac{1}{4}$.
